key_insight: OCP-CT improves CT vision-language pretraining by aligning images and reports at the level of organ-conditioned radiological patterns rather than only at the whole-scan or whole-organ level.
clinical_relevance: This could make zero-shot CT abnormality detection more sensitive to heterogeneous findings across organs, potentially improving downstream radiology decision support.
method: Keeps a global CT-report contrastive branch for stable scan-level alignment
Uses sparse Mixture-of-Experts routing to send image and text tokens to latent radiological patterns
Learns continuous pattern tokens with slots and aligns them using report-derived soft clinical similarity targets
evidence_signal: On CT-RATE and RAD-ChestCT, the method reached average zero-shot abnormality AUROCs of 84.5% and 69.9%, with reported gains of 6.7 and 0.8 points over the strongest prior results.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate report-derived similarity signals and complex token-routing design, so robustness across institutions and annotation styles may need further validation.
paper_title: Fine-Grained Vision-Language Pretraining with Organ-Conditioned Pattern Tokens for CT Understanding
